materials.title: The notebook beside the robot
materials.text:
At our robotics club exhibition, visitors admired the machine that followed a black line across the floor. My friend wrote its code; another designed its body. I stood behind them, unsure what to say about my own ____1____.

For weeks, I had checked batteries, labelled wires and written down what happened during tests. It seemed less ____2____ than making the robot move. When a visitor asked who had built it, I almost said, "They did."

Then the robot stopped halfway along the line. My friend opened the computer, ready to change the ____3____. I remembered an entry in my notebook: the same sudden stop had happened when one battery connection was loose.

"Can we check this first?" I asked. A wire had slipped. Once it was secured, the robot ____4____ its journey.

The visitor turned to me. "How did you know?"

I showed her the notebook. Each test had a date, a description and a drawing of the connections. The pages were not tidy, but they helped us ____5____ today's problem with an earlier one.

Our teacher asked me to put the notebook beside the display. I ____6____, worried that its crossed-out lines would look careless. She said those changes showed what the team had actually tried.

As the afternoon continued, several visitors stopped to read it. One asked why we had ____7____ a larger wheel. I could answer because I had recorded the reason, not just the final choice.

I began to describe my role more ____8____. I had not written the main code, but I had helped keep our learning from ____9____ between tests. The robot's smooth movement depended on more than the parts visitors could ____10____.

My friend requested a copy for our next design. I felt ____11____, but the notes mattered because they helped ____12____. A team needed different kinds of ____13____. I had already been doing a ____14____ job. At the next meeting, I opened a fresh notebook and asked what we needed to ____15____.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 1.
questions.explanation: The narrator is uncertain about their contribution or role. Age, coat and address do not concern who built the robot.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 2.
questions.explanation: Checking and recording feel less exciting than making visible motion. Danger, cost and familiarity are not the comparison motivating insecurity.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 3.
questions.explanation: The friend who programmed it opens the computer to change code. Floor, battery and physical label are not changed through that programming action.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 4.
questions.explanation: Securing the loose wire lets the robot continue. Forgetting, planning or measuring does not resume the halted movement.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 5.
questions.explanation: The dated notes connect the present fault with an earlier event. Hiding or denying prevents diagnosis, while replacing one problem with another is not the task.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 6.
questions.explanation: Concern about crossed-out lines leads to hesitation. Immediate agreement or celebration lacks the uncertainty, and the narrator remains present.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 7.
questions.explanation: The notebook explains a final design choice including rejecting a larger wheel. Buying/painting do not explain its absence, and no accidental loss is described.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 8.
questions.explanation: The narrator can now explain the role with confidence. Quietness and brevity concern delivery mechanics; anger has no supporting cue.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 9.
questions.explanation: Records prevent learning being lost between tests. Growing and starting are desirable, while change itself is not what the notebook prevents.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 10.
questions.explanation: Visitors see the physical machine more readily than the recorded testing work. Weight, borrowing and carrying are not the visible-versus-hidden contribution contrast.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 11.
questions.explanation: A request for the useful notes makes the narrator pleased. Guilt, boredom and loneliness do not fit recognition and continuing collaboration.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 12.
questions.explanation: The team uses the notes for future work, so usefulness to others matters. Customers, judges and strangers are not the identified next-design users.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 13.
questions.explanation: Distinct roles are different contributions to the team. Competition, permission and decoration do not name that cooperative work.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 14.
questions.explanation: The notes prove needed for diagnosis and future design: necessary work. Temporary, private and simple do not capture their importance.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 15.
questions.explanation: A fresh notebook is for recording new tests and decisions. Advertising, erasing and selling do not continue that useful role.

materials.title: A small bowl and a new word
materials.text:
During an exchange visit, I entered a small café alone. The menu was completely ____1____ to me. I tried asking the waiter what she would ____2____, but she shook her head. She could not ____3____ my English question.

For a moment, I felt ____4____. I wanted to leave before making a bigger mistake. The waiter, however, remained ____5____. She brought a pencil and a piece of paper.

I drew a bowl with lines rising from it. My ____6____ was terrible, but she laughed gently and pointed towards a pot behind the counter. Then she drew two bowls of different sizes. I chose the ____7____ one because I was not very hungry.

She wrote a number beside it. This was the ____8____, which I could understand. I ____9____ to show agreement, and she went to the kitchen.

The soup was warm and delicious. As I ate, I felt myself ____10____. A difficult moment had become a small conversation, even though neither of us had suddenly learned the other's language.

Before leaving, I asked her to say the name of the dish slowly. I repeated it until I could say it reasonably well. She wrote it beside my bowl, and I folded the paper into my pocket so I would ____11____ it.

Back with my host family, I showed them the picture. They enjoyed my account of the ____12____ as much as the drawing. The next afternoon, I returned and ordered using my new word. The waiter recognised me and drew a smiling face on the bill.

I still wanted to learn more vocabulary. But I stopped expecting my speech to be ____13____ before trying a simple exchange. A little patience and the ____14____ to ask could open a door. The paper bowl stayed in my travel notebook, reminding me how much a conversation can achieve once we ____15____.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 1.
questions.explanation: The narrator cannot read the language, making the menu unfamiliar. No prices establish expense; a printed menu is not empty and ordinary does not explain the language barrier.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 2.
questions.explanation: Asking which dish to choose is asking for a recommendation. Forget, borrow and repair do not select food from a menu.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 3.
questions.explanation: The waiter cannot understand the spoken English request. Remember and repeat would concern recalling or reproducing words, not grasping the request, while collecting a spoken question is not the activity taking place.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 4.
questions.explanation: Wanting to leave before another mistake shows feeling helpless. Pride and certainty conflict with the insecurity; sleepiness is not described.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 5.
questions.explanation: Bringing drawing materials and working through the request demonstrates patience. Anger, absence and carelessness conflict with her helpful actions.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 6.
questions.explanation: The bowl image is a drawing, later kept as a picture. It is not the cooked meal, written words or voice.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 7.
questions.explanation: Not being hungry motivates the smaller portion. Heavier/larger increase it; depth is not the offered distinction of two drawn sizes.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 8.
questions.explanation: A number beside the chosen dish is its price for the purchase. Date, age and distance do not explain agreeing to the food order.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 9.
questions.explanation: Nodding conveys agreement across the language barrier. Complaining opposes it, hiding avoids communication and running leaves the exchange.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 10.
questions.explanation: Enjoying the food after resolving the difficulty lets the narrator relax. Disappearance is impossible here; rushing and arguing do not match the easing mood.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 11.
questions.explanation: Keeping the written name helps remember it for a later order. Correcting, selling and inventing are not why it is saved.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 12.
questions.explanation: The host family hears about the attempt to communicate. No recipe, weather report or building description is given.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 13.
questions.explanation: The narrator learns to try without complete linguistic perfection. Quietness, privacy and speed are not the standard previously feared.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 14.
questions.explanation: Willingness to ask supplies the initiative needed. Permission, a promise and an order are not the personal readiness described.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 15.
questions.explanation: The lesson values beginning an exchange despite limited words. Waiting or leaving prevents it; payment is one later action rather than the start of conversation.
